$description: D2 examples — nine applicability rules of data/applicability.json raised to v2: three each for the GDPR, the DSA and the AI Act, covering establishment and targeting, public authorities, the platform tiers with their SME exclusions, the VLOP threshold, marketplaces, the prohibitions, the systemic-risk presumption and the two high-risk routes. PROPOSED in v2 Session 2; nothing here is in data/.
$note: ONE HOME. Each example names the rule by id and lists the fields it leaves UNCHANGED instead of copying them: conditions, outcome, rationale, obligations, authority, dates and depends_on stay exactly as they are in data/applicability.json at main 933515a. Only the v2 fields are written out. EVIDENCE. Every locator below was read on 25 Oct 2026 in the Official Journal texts retrieved from the Publications Office's Cellar: GDPR (32016R0679) Arts 2, 3, 4, 30, 37; DSA (32022R2065) Arts 2, 3, 19, 29, 30, 33; AI Act (32024R1689) Arts 2, 3, 6, 51, 53; Digital Omnibus on AI (32026R1744) Art. 1 points (2)–(5), (7), (8) and (40). The AI Act is cited as amended: a locator into the 2024 text is paired with the amending point wherever that point touches the same article, and where it does not (Art. 3 points (3), (4) and (63); Arts 51 and 53) the verification note says so. AMENDMENTS FOUND. Two examples change more than the shape — ap-gdpr-03 gains the courts exception and ap-ai-act-03's threshold key changes comparator — and both are data changes for the author (docs/V2-DATA-DESIGN.md §7, F-4 and F-5).

exemptions.text: Processing by competent authorities for law-enforcement purposes falls under the Law Enforcement Directive rather than the GDPR — an instrument outside this dataset.
Courts acting in their judicial capacity are not required to designate a data protection officer.

basis.locator: Art. 37(1)(a), 'except for courts acting in their judicial capacity'

v2.verification_note: NEW EXEMPTION, a data change for the author (F-5): the rule says a public authority must designate a DPO 'irrespective of the scale of processing', which holds, but Art. 37(1)(a) excepts courts acting in their judicial capacity and the rule does not say so. The GDPR does not define 'public authority'; Art. 37(1)(a) is the provision that uses it for this obligation, hence condition_provisions.actor.

exemptions.text: Micro and small enterprises are exempt from the Section 3 online-platform obligations, except Article 24(3), and for twelve months after losing that status …

v2.verification_note: DATES. The rule lists tl-ai-act-2025-02-02-application only. The Omnibus's new prohibitions in Art. 5(1)(ba)–(bb) apply from 2 December 2026, and data/timeline.json already holds that event (tl-ai-act-2026-12-02-application, introduced_by ai-omnibus) — the rule omits it (F-8). Under v2 the rule's application dates are DERIVED from its obligations and the timeline, so the omission cannot recur. The rationale's 'not affected by the Omnibus deferral' remains true of the original prohibitions and now needs a clause on the new ones: a wording change for the author.

v2.verification_note: COMPARATOR (F-4): Art. 51(2) presumes high-impact capabilities when training compute 'is greater than 10^25' floating-point operations. The v1 key is _gte, which would include a model at exactly 10^25. The matcher reads only the key's presence, so the rename changes no outcome, but the key is what a reader and T-05 check against. Renaming a data key is a data change for the author. Arts 51 and 55 are not amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 (its Art. 1 amends neither). Art. 55 was not re-read.
